name: Ecosystems
blurb: Interdependence, food webs and energy flow between organisms.
whyHard: Students naturally reason in single chains (“more grass → more rabbits”) rather than networks, and struggle to trace effects that are more than one link away — removing a predator changing a plant two steps removed, for instance.
label: Stage 4 · Living systems

name: Designing a first-hand investigation
blurb: Identifying variables and building a fair, repeatable method.
whyHard: Students can often define ‘independent variable’ correctly on a test but still fail to apply the discipline of isolating one variable at a time when they have to build a method themselves.
label: Stage 4–5 · any practical topic

name: Evaluating evidence from secondary sources
blurb: Weighing sample size, methodology and bias; separating correlation from causation.
whyHard: Students tend to judge a claim by how persuasive or familiar it sounds, not by checking the features — sample size, replication, funding — that actually indicate reliability.
label: Stage 5–6 · Nature of Science

name: Chemical equilibrium
blurb: Dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier’s principle.
whyHard: Almost every student starts by picturing equilibrium as a reaction that has stopped, rather than one still running in both directions at equal rates — and the misconception often survives correct-sounding definitions.
label: Stage 6 · Chemistry
